judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all fees, costs and expenses (including fees paid for consulting and financial services)' is broad but the category is anchored to the defined 'Transactions'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02(d) permits Loan proceeds to be used for 'the Project's costs and Transaction Costs amounts', which depends on this definition; the two are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb (b), 'the completion and operations of the Project and any matters related thereto', is an unbounded tail that swallows limb (a)'s careful enumeration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Transaction Costs' and the Adjusted Net Income accrual carve-outs both key off this term, so its breadth propagates, though no direct contradiction appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition ends in vagueness of its own making: 'certain of which Unsecured Subordinated Promoter Loans are excluded from certain definitions as used herein' identifies neither the loans nor the definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The term is in fact excluded from Adjusted Tangible Net Worth, Net Debt, Long-Term Debt and Total Debt, so the 'certain definitions' language must be reconciled with four specific provisions, and the reference to 'Section G.07' does not correspond to a numbered section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise arithmetic definition subtracting funded Loans and outstanding LC Exposure from the Commitment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the operative cap in Sections 2.01, 2.03(a), 2.06(a) and 2.06(b) and the thing cancelled under Section 2.08(a); all of those uses are consistent with this arithmetic.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It names two institutions but then makes their status conditional on provisos (a) and (b) requiring identical terms 'including principal amount, interest rate, repayment and prepayment terms and events of default', a demanding and self-defeating standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: They are Secured Parties sharing pari passu under 'Secured Party' and are given prepayment rights under the pro rata definitions, so the conditional status has knock-on effects for those provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The closing phrase 'on the same terms as the required by the Loans' is grammatically broken, and the whole fraction is conditional on whether other creditors 'require' a mandatory prepayment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is keyed to Section 2.11(f) while the parallel 'Lender's Pro Rata Interest' is keyed to Section 2.11(b), an inconsistency across definitions that are meant to allocate the same prepayment pot.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'other de minimis amounts of outstanding securities or ownership interests' is a soft carve-out inside an otherwise 100% test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the lower-case 'subsidiary' definition and with 'Investment'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure statutory cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Multiemployer Plan' and limb (h) of 'ERISA Event'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'or other institutional lender' is a mild general tail after two specifics, with an express Affiliate exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Working Capital Bank Financing' and the Security Agreement's Current Assets subordination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a secured or unsecured working capital facility' with no cap, no tenor and an 'including' extension to receivables sales, leaves the category almost entirely open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Security Agreement definition subordinates the Secured Parties' Current Assets security to this financing once permitted under Section 6.01, and 'Total Debt' refers to it by the wrong name ('Working Capital Bank Finance'), so its perimeter matters and is imperfectly tracked.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard set of interpretive conventions; each rule is stated flatly and the deeming provisions ('include' means 'without limitation'; 'will' means 'shall') remove rather than create ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'without limitation' rule expands every 'including' catch-all elsewhere, notably in Section 2.08(a)'s 'for any reason, including', which is a consequence the drafters presumably intended.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in accordance with and consistent with prior years practice' is an undefined overlay on GAAP, and the two nested provisos about frozen GAAP and reconciliations are hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies GAAP to the Borrower and IFRS to the Guarantors, which must be squared with the 'GAAP' and 'IFRS' definitions and with the many financial definitions expressed 'in accordance with GAAP'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The section states the maximum amount 'available' rather than any promise to lend, and 'Subject to the terms and conditions set forth herein' leaves the availability entirely conditional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says undrawn Commitments 'lapse automatically at the end of the Term Loan Availability Period', yet Section 2.06 allows Letters of Credit whose disbursements automatically convert into Term Loans well after that date, and Section 2.08(a) lets any Lender cancel its Unused Commitment for any reason at any time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cross-reference reads 'as contemplated by clauses (i) above', mixing plural and singular, and the sub-facility structure ties availability to conditions in sections not reproduced.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Tranche A-2 covers 'the remaining amount of the Initial Lender Tranche A Total Commitment', but Section 2.02(b) also makes that same remaining amount available under Tranche B on different conditions, so the two overlap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical '(and any remaining amount of the Initial Lender Tranche A Total Commitment to the extent not previously borrowed)' grafts Tranche A money onto Tranche B without saying which tranche's conditions and limits then govern it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.02(a)(ii) already makes that remaining Tranche A amount available on satisfaction of Sections 4.02 and 4.04, whereas this paragraph conditions it on Financial Closure and Sections 4.03 and 4.04, producing two different condition sets for the same money.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short deferral to the Accession Agreement with no operative content of its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 'Accession Project Financing', 'Term Loan Commitment' and 'Total Commitment', all of which defer to Section 2.20.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the payment of the Project's costs and Transaction Costs amounts' is ungrammatical, and 'the Project's costs' has no defined content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The prohibition on using proceeds to fund the DSRA has to be read with Section 2.06(j), which directs cash collateral into the DSRA, and with Section 2.05, which routes all Loan proceeds through the Escrow Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short paragraph with one proviso; 'as it may deem appropriate' is discretionary but on the Borrower's side and cabined by the Commitment cap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes that a Lender to whom a request is made must fund, which sits against Section 2.08(a)'s unilateral cancellation right and Section 2.04's statement that Lenders have 'no obligation' if the Eurodollar rate is unavailable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: There is a stray period mid-sentence ('required to be made by it . shall not relieve'), but the several-liability rule itself is stated twice and clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to Loans 'required to be made', which assumes a funding obligation that Section 2.08(a) allows any Lender to extinguish for any reason on notice.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'each Borrowing shall be comprised entirely of Eurodollar Rate Borrowings' is circular, since a Borrowing cannot be comprised of Borrowings, and 'Eurodollar Rate Borrowing' is itself defined as a description of Loans.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.04 repeats that each Borrowing shall be a Eurodollar Rate Borrowing and then contemplates funding 'at a different rate of interest' in the Lenders' complete discretion under Section 2.14, so the 'entirely' rule is not absolute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in an amount of not less than ten million Dollars ... in not more than fifteen (15) Borrowings' does not say whether the fifteen-Borrowing limit is per Lender, per tranche or in total.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.03(a) permits requests from one or more Lenders in different amounts and Section 2.02 splits the facility into tranches, which makes the unallocated fifteen-Borrowing cap harder to apply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening sentence is garbled ('shall notify the Facility Agent and the Escrow Agent and Account Bank of such request and in writing not later than'), and the closing passage says the Lenders 'may' fund but 'shall have no obligation to do so ... in their complete discretion'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That discretion sits against Section 2.05's 'Each Lender shall make each Loan to be made by it hereunder' and against the recital that the Initial Lender is willing to provide the Facilities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The funding obligation is stated flatly with a time and a destination, and the consequential-damages waiver is a single clear sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mandatory 'Each Lender shall make each Loan' has to be reconciled with Section 2.08(a)'s right to cancel Unused Commitments 'for any reason' and with Section 2.04's statement that Lenders have no obligation to fund where the Eurodollar rate is unavailable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence with three nested qualifications and a proviso, in which the phrase 'as reduced by any Borrowings under Section 2.02(a) or (b)' is left dangling between two long clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Letters of Credit may be requested to 30 June 2013, which is inside the Term Loan Availability Period, but their conversion into Term Loans can occur after the Commitments lapse under Section 2.01.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The documentary requirements are listed as alternatives (i) to (v) joined by 'or' and then closed by '(vi) such other documents as may be specified by the Issuing Bank from time to time', a catch-all that swallows the enumerated list; 'reasonably acceptable in form and substance' adds a further soft filter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The deemed representation about LC Exposure not exceeding the Unused Commitment uses 'LC Exposure' in an Issuing-Bank-aggregate sense that does not match the Lender-level limb of the 'LC Exposure' definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-limb 'first to occur' rule stated with dates and no soft language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 'Letter of Credit' definition states the same expiry rule and then adds that 'the last date of negotiation of any letter of credit shall not be later than December 30, 2014', which is after the four-year outside date of 29 December 2014 produced by this paragraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conversion trigger depends on the Issuing Bank having 'not less than five (5) Business Days' prior notice of such LC Disbursement' without saying from whom, and the second sentence measures the same five days from receipt of documentation instead, giving two different clocks.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to work with Section 2.06(h)'s interim interest, with the 'LC Exposure' definition's carve-out for disbursements 'converted to Term Loans pursuant to Section 2.06(e)', and with Section 2.01's automatic lapse of Commitments.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph makes obligations absolute 'irrespective of ... (iii) any other event or circumstance whatsoever', then carves back liability for the Issuing Bank's 'failure to exercise care', and then deems care to have been exercised absent gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, so the standard of care is stated twice inconsistently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.06(g) says the Issuing Bank has 'the final word' and the Borrower 'will not question its decision' absent gross negligence, which pulls against the direct-damages carve-out preserved here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Issuing Bank will have the final word' is colloquial and undefined, and 'if, or if not, determined credit compliant the Borrower will not question its decision' is grammatically broken to the point that its scope is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Section 2.06(f), which expressly preserves the Borrower's claim for direct damages caused by the Issuing Bank's failure to exercise care in determining documentary compliance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'shall be payable immediately on demand by the Borrower' is ambiguous as to whether the Borrower makes or receives the demand, and interest is stated to be 'for the account of the applicable Issuing Bank' which may not be the Lender bearing the exposure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Section 2.06(e)'s automatic conversion timing and with 'Interest Payment Date', which fixes interest payment at the end of an Interest Period rather than on demand.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger conflates acceleration with automatic insolvency defaults and then says the amount is payable 'immediately ... without demand or other notice of any kind', while the return mechanism assumes Events of Default can be cured after acceleration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cash is deposited into the DSRA, whereas Section 2.02(d) forbids using proceeds to fund or maintain the DSRA, and the deposit is said to secure 'the Obligations' although the security package runs to Secured Obligations under the Security Documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumeration runs '(i) ... and (iii)' with no clause (ii), the same defect as in the 'Interest Period' definition, and the concept of an Interest Period 'shall be for an Interest Period' is circular.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the second half of the 'Interest Period' definition almost word for word, including the missing (ii), so the two provisions replicate rather than resolve each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences; the only oddity is treating the election as something made 'in' the first Borrowing Request while also naming a separate Interest Election Request.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Interest Election Request' is defined as a distinct 'one-time request' and Section 2.07(c) speaks of the Facility Agent receiving it, yet this paragraph says the election is made inside the Borrowing Request under Section 2.04.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short notification mechanic with no discretionary or vague language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It assumes a standalone Interest Election Request, consistent with the definition but less so with Section 2.07(b)'s embedding of the election in the Borrowing Request.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short override clause pointing to Section 2.13(c) for default interest.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.13 is outside the produced text, so the referenced default-rate mechanism cannot be checked, but nothing in Article II contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph says cancellation may be 'for any reason, including the deterioration in the Borrower's creditworthiness due to (i)-(iii)', a general power followed by three specifics whose relationship is uncertain, and it requires 'prior written notice' while allowing cancellation 'immediately upon such notice' and then only that Lenders 'shall endeavor to provide prior notice'; 'deterioration in the Borrower's creditworthiness' is itself undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot easily be reconciled with Section 2.05's 'Each Lender shall make each Loan to be made by it hereunder', with Section 2.03(b)'s reference to Loans 'required to be made', with the availability regime in Sections 2.01 and 2.02, or with the recital that the Initial Lender 'is willing to provide the Facilities'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Borrower's right depends on whether 'the Project costs shall have been reduced below one billion ninety seven million Dollars', with no definition of Project costs and no mechanism for determining or verifying the reduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That figure comes only from the recital, where it is 'currently estimated to be approximately' US$1,097,000,000, so an operative right turns on a recital estimate; it also contrasts with Section 2.08(a), which gives Lenders an unconditional cancellation right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text says repayment is in 'twenty-three (23) approximately equal installments, and with the remaining amount outstanding in the twenty-fourth (24th) installment' while the table sets 24 dated percentages, and the Business Day proviso directs payment on the 'next preceding' Business Day, which for the 1 January dates moves payment into the prior year.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final installment must be paid on the Term Loan Maturity Date of 1 January 2020, which is not a Business Day, so the preceding-Business-Day proviso and the maturity requirement point to different dates; the amortisation is also measured from the last day of the Term Loan Availability Period even though LC Disbursements can convert into Term Loans afterwards.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence record-keeping obligation keyed to each Lender's usual practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It pairs with the Facility Agent's register in Section 2.10(b); nothing conflicts.
